title: You Don't Need More Time, You Need Less Time
contributor: A mother of two who learned to work in windows
pullQuote: The 'more time' I'd been craving was actually the very thing keeping me unfocused.

paragraphs: Before I had my first child, I lived in the 'I wish I had more time' trap. I convinced myself that if I only had a few more hours, I'd finally master that skill, finish that project, or find true balance.

Then motherhood hit, and my time didn't just shrink — it evaporated. But a strange thing happened: as my available hours decreased, my output soared. I realized that the 'more time' I'd been craving was actually the very thing keeping me unfocused.

sections.heading: The Power of the Hard Stop
paragraphs: When I started dropping my baby at daycare, my day suddenly gained a border. My focus window became a strict 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM.

In my old life, time was an endless, blurry expanse. I could afford to let a task drift into the evening or lose an hour to noise. But with a 5:30 PM pickup looming, the noise died out. My brain switched from wandering to executing. Whatever needed my attention got it immediately, because there was no 'later' to fall back on.

sections.heading: The 'Less Time' Achievement
paragraphs: It sounds counterintuitive, but I achieved more by having less. Before my daughter turned one — within that compressed 9-to-5:30 window — I hit two massive milestones: a promotion at my tech company, and producing and releasing my own music videos.

The constraint acted like a lens. It took the scattered energy of my ambition and focused it into a laser. By the time I had my second child, the lesson was cemented: life doesn't stop when time gets tight. It just gets clearer.

sections.heading: Shift Your Perspective
paragraphs: We often view 'less time' as a deficit, but it's actually a tool for clarity. If you find yourself wishing for more hours, try shifting your perspective. Instead of seeking more time to do things, seek less time to focus. When your window is small, you don't have the luxury of procrastination. You only have the space for what truly matters.
Stop waiting for a 30-hour day. Start using your eight hours like they're the only ones you've got.
What would you prioritize today if your work window closed two hours earlier?

whatLearned: That constraints are not the enemy of ambition — they are the sharpest tool it has. Motherhood didn't shrink my life. It focused it.
